Computes the unit or cohort level sequential synthetic diff-in-diff or diff-in-diff estimate.

sequential_estimator.Rd

Basically, this function is a wrapper which calls either estimation_cohort or estimation_unit function. Then it aggregates the

Usage

sequential_estimator(
  panel_avg,
  level = NULL,
  s2 = NULL,
  type = "sdid",
  aggregate_effect = aggregate_inv_did_var
)

Arguments

panel_avg

: List. The list should contain:

  • Y_avg: Numeric matrix. The N x T matrix of outcomes.

  • W_avg: Binary or boolen matrix. The N x T matrix of treatment indicators. The matrix has a stair-like structure with treated cells being at the bottom.

  • coh: Numeric vector. The Nx1 cohort weights vector (the number of units in cohorts or the cohort population).

  • X: Dataframe. The dataframe is not aggregated to cohort and covariate level. It contains auxiliary data like adoption date, population weights and covariates.

level

: Character or NULL. If NULL, the level is taken from panel_avg list. The level should be unit or cohort.

s2

: Numeric or NULL. The upper bound estimate of noise variance.

type

: Character. Type of the estimator should be sdid, did or both.

aggregate_effect

: Function. The function aggregates the treatment effect for every lag by weighting the effect for every cohort. The function should contain the following arguments:

  • tau: Numeric matrix or array.

  • W: Numeric matrix.

  • coh: Numeric vector.

  • N0: Integer. The number of control (never-treated) units.

  • N: Integer. The total number of units.

return_s2

: Bool. If TRUE, returns s2. If s2 is not passed (NULL), s2 is estimated and returned.

Value

              sequential_estimator
